content.user_title: Plan a healthier renovation with clear material guidance
content.value_statement: Renovation choices can involve confusing pollution claims and conflicting material advice. This skill organizes reference-based questions into practical checks for materials, ventilation, and household needs.
actual_capabilities: Asks about household members before suggesting renovation priorities.
Explains the total-materials approach to indoor pollution risk.
Compares common wall, floor, cabinet, and adhesive material choices.
Explains common claims about formaldehyde treatment and consumer testing.
Offers non-brand-specific alternatives for lower-material renovation plans.
limitations: It provides general educational guidance, not medical, legal, or laboratory advice.
It does not inspect a property, test air quality, or verify product certificates.
Its recommendations rely on bundled reference material and may not reflect local regulations.
It does not recommend brands, merchants, or specific products.

use_cases.title: Plan a child-friendly room
use_cases.description: Identify material and furnishing choices to discuss with a renovation team before work begins.

use_cases.title: Compare cabinet options
use_cases.description: Review board types, material quantity, and alternative storage approaches for a renovation plan.

use_cases.title: Question pollution-control claims
use_cases.description: Prepare focused questions when evaluating ventilation, testing, or formaldehyde-treatment claims.

prompt_templates.title: Start with a room plan
prompt_templates.prompt: I am renovating a bedroom. Ask about my household, then give a simple environmental material checklist.

prompt_templates.title: Choose cabinet materials
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare my options for custom cabinets. Explain how board type, quantity, and edge sealing affect my renovation plan.

prompt_templates.title: Review a proposed materials list
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this planned list of floors, wall finishes, cabinets, and adhesives. Identify where material quantity may increase indoor pollution concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Challenge a contractor claim
prompt_templates.prompt: A contractor says this treatment guarantees formaldehyde removal. Help me assess the claim and prepare evidence-based follow-up questions.

output_examples.input: I have a young child and plan many built-in cabinets. What should I consider?
output: The skill first asks about the room, ventilation, and move-in schedule.
It then explains material quantity, cabinet choices, and alternatives to discuss with the contractor.

output_examples.input: Is wallpaper better than paint for indoor air quality?
output: The skill compares the relevant materials and installation components.
It highlights that the overall material system matters, not a single marketing label.

best_practices: Share household needs, rooms, materials, and move-in timing before asking for recommendations.
Use the guidance to prepare questions for qualified local professionals and suppliers.
Check current local standards and independent documentation before making purchase decisions.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the skill as a substitute for a site inspection or accredited measurement.
Do not rely on a single label or brand claim as proof of a healthy indoor environment.
Do not use the guidance to make urgent health decisions without qualified professional support.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps users discuss renovation materials, pollution claims, ventilation, and household-specific planning.

faq.question: Can it test formaldehyde levels?
faq.answer: No. It cannot inspect a home or perform laboratory or on-site measurements.

faq.question: Does it recommend brands?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on material categories and questions to ask rather than specific sellers or products.

faq.question: Who is it for?
faq.answer: It is for homeowners who want structured guidance before or during a renovation.

faq.question: Will it replace professional advice?
faq.answer: No. Use it as educational support alongside qualified local professionals when needed.

faq.question: What information should I provide?
faq.answer: Share the household members, rooms, materials planned, ventilation conditions, and move-in schedule.
